questions.title: If the Boston Celtics agree to trade Jaylen Brown by July 31, 2026, which NBA team will be his destination?
questions.background: Jaylen Brown plays for the Boston Celtics and was named the 2024 NBA Finals MVP.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Reporting by ESPN or The Associated Press identifying an agreed trade involving Jaylen Brown between June 1 and July 31, 2026. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the team designated to receive Brown under the first such publicly reported agreement. An agreement counts even if league approval or completion remains pending. Accepted Answer Format : The full name of the NBA team.
questions.current_reasoning: After Boston's offer of Jaylen Brown and two unprotected first-round picks lost out to Miami in the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade on June 22-23, ESPN's Shams Charania and Brian Windhorst reported on June 23 that the Celtics are actively taking calls and a bidding war could develop for Brown ($57.1M salary in 2026-27, extension-eligible July 26). Conditional on a trade occurring by July 31, NBC Sports, Marc Stein, and Bleacher Report identify the Houston Rockets and Atlanta Hawks as the clear frontrunners, with the Portland Trail Blazers, Los Angeles Clippers, and New Orleans Pelicans also linked as active suitors. Because NBA superstar trades frequently land with surprise or secondary suitors due to second-apron salary-matching constraints, 33% probability mass is left on the remaining 24 NBA teams.

questions.title: Which NBA team will sign Trey Alexander to a two-way contract in the first two weeks of July 2026?
questions.background: A two-way contract allows a player to play for both an NBA team and its G League affiliate.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : as confirmed by a team announcement or contemporaneous sports reporting Resolution Date : Resolve to the NBA team that signs Trey Alexander to a two-way contract between July 1 and July 14, 2026, inclusive Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the team's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Trey Alexander (2024-25 G League Rookie of the Year with Denver) spent 2025-26 on a one-year two-way contract with the New Orleans Pelicans, shooting 51.4% FG and 50.0% 3PT in 9 NBA games while playing mainly for Birmingham, and enters the 2026 offseason as a Pelicans restricted two-way free agent per Spotrac. Incumbent RFA rights give New Orleans by far the highest single-team probability (32%) of re-signing him via qualifying offer or new two-way deal in early July, though coaching turnover and post-draft roster cycling leave a ~68% chance he signs elsewhere as Denver let him walk on July 3, 2025. questions.title: Which company will hold the record for the largest US IPO by a foreign firm as of July 10, 2026?
questions.background: Alibaba's 2014 US initial public offering raised $25 billion, setting the record for the largest US IPO by a foreign company.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official issuer announcements and contemporaneous reporting by reputable news organizations. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the company reported as holding the all-time record for the largest US initial public offering by a foreign company as of July 10, 2026. Compare offerings by proceeds raised, not company valuation. An offering whose pricing and share sales have been announced may qualify before exchange trading begins. Accepted Answer Format : The company's commonly used name.
questions.current_reasoning: On June 24, 2026, South Korea's SK Hynix filed to raise up to 45.45 trillion won (~$29.4 billion) via a Nasdaq ADR offering of 17.79 million new shares, with bookbuilding slated to start July 7 and pricing and Nasdaq debut expected on July 10—explicitly targeting Alibaba's 2014 $25B ($21.8B pre-greenshoe) foreign U.S. listing record. Strong AI memory demand (HBM sold out into 2027, BofA/Citi/GS/JPM managing) and the resolution rule allowing announced pricing prior to trading make SK Hynix the clear favorite. However, Alibaba retains a substantial ~37% chance because the 16-day SEC Form F-1 schedule could slip past July 10, elevated Korean/Nasdaq tech volatility plus an ADR pricing discount could pull proceeds under $25B, or reporting could distinguish an already-listed firm's ADR offering from a traditional IPO.

questions.background: Tarik Skubal is a starting pitcher for the Detroit Tigers and is eligible for free agency after the 2026 season.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official MLB or team announcements, or confirmed reporting from ESPN, identifying a completed trade of Tarik Skubal by the 2026 MLB trade deadline. Resolution : Resolve to the MLB club acquiring Skubal directly from the Detroit Tigers. If no such trade occurs by the deadline, the question is void. questions.current_reasoning: With the Detroit Tigers far out of contention and pending free agent Tarik Skubal (3.02 ERA, 1.02 WHIP) owed ~$9M remaining, ESPN, CBS Sports, and USA Today report Detroit is likely to deal him before the Aug. 3 deadline for controllable MLB-ready pitching and close-to-MLB bats. Conditional on a completed trade, the Los Angeles Dodgers are the consensus frontrunner (24%) given their unmatched controllable-arm depth (e.g., Emmet Sheehan), Glasnow/Snell 60-day IL injuries, and three-peat urgency. The New York Yankees (14%, rotation injuries and Nightengale/MLB.com top-four listing), Atlanta Braves (11%, Strider elbow injury and aggressive GM Alex Anthopoulos), Chicago Cubs (9%, highly rated ESPN package and rotation injuries), and Toronto Blue Jays (7%, named among rival execs' top four by Nightengale) lead a wide contender field with 35% mass left on clubs like the Padres, Phillies, Brewers, Mets, and Orioles.

questions.title: Who will win the Most Valuable Player award at the 2026 MLB All-Star Game?
questions.background: The MLB All-Star Game is an annual exhibition between the American League and National League. Its Most Valuable Player award recognizes an individual player's performance in the game.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : MLB's official announcement of the 2026 All-Star Game MVP, corroborated by contemporaneous reputable news reporting. Resolution Timing : The question resolves when the MVP recipient is publicly announced following the 2026 All-Star Game, expected in July 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The full name of the player awarded the game's MVP honor.
questions.current_reasoning: The 2026 MLB All-Star Game is July 14 at hitter-friendly Citizens Bank Park in Philadelphia, and as a single-game exhibition featuring ~60 players, even the top MVP favorites carry only 4%-7% true probability (leaving ~73% on the rest of the field). As of the June 22 Phase 1 voting update, Shohei Ohtani leads all of MLB (2.31M votes) as a locked-in NL DH starter with strong voter bias, while Yordan Alvarez (1.97M votes, 25 HRs, 191 OPS+) and Bobby Witt Jr. (1.70M votes) are runaway AL starting locks. MLB home run leader Kyle Schwarber (29 HRs, Phillies hometown crowd favorite despite minor June 23 back tightness and likely reserve role behind Ohtani) and resurgent two-time ASG MVP Mike Trout (1.74M votes, Philadelphia-area native) round out the top five ahead of Aaron Judge, who has been dealing with a June injury.

questions.title: Which Federal Reserve policymakers will vote for an interest-rate increase at the July 29, 2026 FOMC meeting?
questions.background: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) sets US monetary policy. Its policy announcements disclose members' votes and the policy preferences of dissenting voters.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Federal Reserve's official policy statement and voting record for the meeting concluding July 29, 2026, corroborated by contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution : Identify every voting member whose recorded position favors increasing the federal funds target range relative to the range immediately before the meeting. Include those members whether an increase is adopted or they dissent in favor of one. Accepted Answer Format : All qualifying members' surnames, listed alphabetically and separated by commas.
questions.current_reasoning: At Chair Kevin Warsh's June 17, 2026 FOMC debut, the Committee voted 12-0 to hold at 3.50%-3.75% while removing its easing bias as May inflation surpassed 4.2% and 9 of 18 participants projected at least one 2026 hike (6 saw 2+). In April 2026, rotating 2026 voters Beth Hammack (Cleveland), Neel Kashkari (Minneapolis), and Lorie Logan (Dallas) all dissented together on the hawkish side, and both Hammack ('soon appropriate to act') and Logan ('higher interest rates could be necessary') issued strongly hawkish June remarks. While a July 29 hold remains the base case—especially with oil falling on U.S.-Iran talks—hawkish dissents for a 25bp hike by combinations of Hammack, Logan, Kashkari, and Governor Michelle Bowman are highly live depending on June 25 PCE and July 14 CPI; 48% probability remains outside these five exact strings (including a 12-0 hold with zero hike voters, a majority hike, or other combinations).
